text: DSH Context Saver 是一款适用于 DSH Web 客户端的上下文精简插件。它在模型请求发送前拦截 llm/stream，并按设置重建消息；本地会话记录保持完整。它可以清空思考块文本、折叠重复文件或网页读取、移除终端调用参数，也可精简对话中部回合。用户可在输入框工具栏打开中英双语面板控制开关与保留回合数。默认启用思考内容和重复读取精简；终端参数与中部回合精简默认关闭。不需要额外 API Key 或账号。

DSH Context Saver trims context sent to models while keeping local history. It clears reasoning, collapses repeated reads, removes terminal arguments, or trims middle turns. A bilingual composer panel controls options. No extra API key is required.
想减少每次发给模型的上下文里重复的文件和网页读取内容。
能不能只精简模型收到的历史，同时保留本地完整会话？
How can I shorten long chat context sent to the model without deleting my local conversation history?
DSH Context Saver 的功能「发送前精简上下文」：在模型请求发送时按开关清空思考文本、折叠重复读取、清除终端调用参数，或清空保留窗口之外的中部回合内容；这些操作只作用于发出的消息副本，本地会话记录继续保留。
DSH Context Saver 的功能「上下文控制面板」：点击对话输入框工具栏中的插件按钮，可切换思考内容、重复读取、终端参数和中部回合精简，并在启用中部精简时设置开头与结尾保留的回合数。

dsh-context-saver README · dsh-context-saver · DSH context saving plugin：A send-time context trimmer for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness).

It trims only at the moment the context is submitted to the model. The local session log, the chat transcript, and the trajectory view stay complete. With the plugin disabled, or with every option off, the request is byte-identical to the untrimmed one.

dsh-context-saver README · What it is for：This plugin removes that material from the **outbound copy** only; the local copy keeps everything.

dsh-context-saver README · How it works：Every model request in DSH passes through the `llm/stream` waterfall, which carries the complete `messages` about to be submitted.

The plugin takes the request there, builds a new message array from the enabled rules, and re-dispatches it with `ctx.llm.stream()`. The original request is deep-frozen and is never modified, and no session event is ever written, so:

dsh-context-saver README · Why the result cannot make DeepSeek reject the request：The DeepSeek Messages adapter imposes hard structural rules. Every shape this plugin emits was designed around them and verified against the live API:
section: Why the result cannot make DeepSeek reject the request

text:
dsh-context-saver README · Why the result cannot make DeepSeek reject the request：| Risk | Handling | Verified |
|---|---|---|
| a `tool_result` without its `tool_use` | `tool-call` blocks are **never removed**, only `arguments` becomes `{}` | accepted |
| a `tool_use` without an immediate result | `tool` role messages are **never removed**, only their content is emptied | accepted |
| thinking block count out of step with local replay metadata | `reasoning` blocks are **never removed**, only `text` is emptied and the signature kept | accepted |
| an empty thinking block rejected | the real signature is still sent | accepted (empty + signature, empty without signature, and no thinking block all return 200) |
section: Why the result cannot make DeepSeek reject the request

text: dsh-context-saver README · Why the result cannot make DeepSeek reject the request：Compaction and session-title requests (`purpose` set) are never trimmed, so their own input cannot change underneath them.
section: Why the result cannot make DeepSeek reject the request

text: dsh-context-saver README · Interface：The control sits in the composer tool row, next to the model and sandbox selectors. Clicking it opens a floating panel:

dsh-context-saver README · Interface：- **Master switch** (on by default)
- **Strip thinking content** (on by default) — keeps each think block, empties its text, so the model receives the answer without the reasoning
- **Strip repeated reads** (on by default) — identical file and page reads keep only the first copy; later ones keep an identifier and an empty structure
- **Strip terminal inputs and process** (off by default) — terminal tool calls keep their output and lose the model-supplied arguments
- **Strip the middle of the context** (off by default) — turning it on raises a warning: *"Stripping the middle of the context can remove important content from the middle of a long conversation while it is being sent!"*
- **Leading turns kept** (5 by default, effective only with middle stripping on)
- **Trailing turns kept** (5 by default, effective only with middle stripping on)

dsh-context-saver README · Interface：The panel is localized in Chinese and English and follows the DSH language setting. Settings are stored on this machine and apply to every session:

```
$DSH_HOME/dsh-context-saver/settings.json
```

The switch track uses a fixed mid-green (on, `#22c55e`) and neutral grey (off, `#9aa0a6`) rather than the theme's `brand-primary` / `border-l2`: in the dark theme those two aliases resolve to a near-white `#f9fafb` and a translucent white, so a white knob on them shows no visible state.

dsh-context-saver README · Middle stripping rule：**One turn is one user message plus the model output that follows it**, so turn boundaries are the `user` messages.

With `N` turns in total, `H` leading turns kept, and `T` trailing turns kept:

dsh-context-saver README · Middle stripping rule：- when `N ≤ H + T` nothing is stripped at all (the two retention windows overlap);
- otherwise a turn is stripped only when it is inside neither window. A stripped turn keeps its structure and loses its content: tool calls keep their id and name with empty arguments, reasoning blocks keep their position and signature with empty text, text and images are cleared, so tool calls and results stay paired.

dsh-context-saver README · Middle stripping rule：Example: 17 turns, 7 leading, 8 trailing → turns 1–7 and 10–17 are kept and turns 8 and 9 are stripped (`7 + 8 = 15` turns retained).

> At least one turn is always kept at each end. The trailing turn carries the current question — emptying it would send a request with no question in it — and the leading one keeps the request starting on a user message. A configured `0` is raised to `1`.

dsh-context-saver README · Measured on real sessions：Two independent measurements, both against the live `deepseek-flash` endpoint.

**A real 65-turn session log from this machine**, replayed through the adapter's own serialization rules with the session's own 34 tool declarations:

| | Prompt tokens | Reply |
|---|---|---|
| Untrimmed | 867,787 | accepted |
| **Trimmed (defaults)** | **574,347** | accepted |

33.8% fewer prompt tokens on a long agentic session, and the model still answered correctly.

dsh-context-saver README · Measured on real sessions：**A 60-turn synthetic session with heavy repeated reads**, comparing the request for turn N against the request for turn N+1 to measure prefix reuse:

| Configuration | Prompt tokens | Cache hit rate |
|---|---|---|
| Trimming off | 21,102 | 98.9% |
| **Defaults** (thinking + repeated reads) | **3,242** | **94.8%** |
| Defaults + terminal | 3,242 | 94.8% |
| Defaults + terminal + middle | 1,847 | 90.1% |

dsh-context-saver README · Measured on real sessions：So the default configuration sends **6.5× fewer prompt tokens at a 94.8% cache hit rate** — the "90% or better" goal holds for every configuration.

dsh-context-saver README · KV cache and hit rate：- Stripped older turns are never rewritten, and new turns are only appended, so the shared prefix stays stable.
- The duplicate marker is a fixed string naming a stable ordinal ("the Nth tool result"), so it does not drift as the session grows. A read shorter than 200 characters is left alone, because the marker would cost more than it saves.
- With middle stripping on, a turn slides from the trailing window into the middle; at that moment its content is cleared and the prefix cache misses once from there. That cost is inherent to any middle-stripping scheme and does not exist while the option is off — hence the lower 90.1% figure.
- The trimmed shape is deterministic, so a retry or a repeated step reuses the cache exactly: two identical requests both measured 95.1%.

dsh-context-saver README · From GitHub：```sh
dsh plugin add github:DaVinci-2nd/dsh-context-saver
```

Pin a commit for a reproducible install: `dsh plugin add github:DaVinci-2nd/dsh-context-saver#<sha>`.

The package is plain JavaScript with no build step and no `prepare` script, so a git install needs **no `allowBuilds` permission**.
dsh-context-saver README · From a local checkout：Choose the directory in the plugin manager, or point `install_bundle` at it.

dsh-context-saver README · The installed row：```yaml
- insert:
    - id: dsh-context-saver
      name: dsh-context-saver
```
dsh-context-saver README · Uninstall：Remove that row, or uninstall the bundle from the plugin manager. The settings file can be deleted by hand.

dsh-context-saver README · Layout：| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `index.js` | Host half: the `llm/stream` interception and the settings route |
| `src/trim.js` | Pure trimming logic, side-effect free and unit tested |
| `src/settings.js` | Defaults and settings persistence |
| `client.js` | Browser half: the composer-row control and its floating panel |
| `locale/*.json` | Plugin Manager title and description (zh / en) |
| `test/trim.test.mjs` | Trimming tests |

dsh-context-saver README · Test：```bash
node test/trim.test.mjs
```
